Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-3-prompt-long-0026", "row_sha256": "1252daa7d5df282f010ce090787edc7d0f76a86e2322ad11dc3ef7ec39027926", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "make me a practical internal handoff note about the shared studio access list, not a message to members and not an update to the actual list. it is for the next person covering the front desk on thursday, april 18. the studio is called North Window Studio and it's on the second floor of the Calder Building. the access list is for the studio room, not the building entrance, so please keep those separate in the note. the building uses badge access at the lobby door; studio keys are handled separately. the note should help the desk person understand what to check and what not to assume, without deciding anything that isn't in these details.

we use a shared workbook, on the tab called Access - Main. the workbook is internal. there is also a printed copy in the clear sleeve beside the inner office door, but that printout can be a day behind, so check the workbook before relying on the paper one. the last date typed at the top of the tab is april 16. don't call that a confirmation that every entry was reviewed that day; it is only the date shown there. if the two copies disagree, mention the mismatch in the handoff and use the workbook as the reference for what is currently written. don't silently change either copy just to make them match.

list has a few different columns and people sometimes read them as if they're the same thing. names are in column a, building badge status in b, studio key status in c, and notes in d. there's a narrow column e marked “checked by,” but several rows are blank there. a blank checked-by cell doesn't mean someone has no key; it means nobody's name is entered in that cell. likewise a name appearing in the sheet doesn't by itself prove their badge or key is active. say this plainly in the handoff, and don't infer a status from an empty cell or from the printed list. some rows have “hold” in notes, which is a note to ask the access lead before changing that row, not an instruction to remove the person.

people/details to include so the handoff has useful examples: Mira Chen's row says badge active, studio key issued, checked by Sal on april 12. Leon Ortiz's row says badge active, key returned, and notes says “returned to drawer 3 on april 15.” Priya Nair is listed with badge pending and studio key blank; her notes say “orientation booked for april 22.” Darius Bell's row has badge active, key issued, and “hold — confirm with Jo” in notes; checked by is blank. don't convert pending into active, and don't say the orientation has already happened. the quote from the front desk log is: “I thought my key was still active.” we don't know who said it from the excerpt, so don't attach it to any of those four people. It's just a reported comment, not proof of status.

for the next shift, the normal task is to check the workbook against any access request already sent through the studio's internal request form, then record only a change that has been confirmed by the access lead. nobody should use the handoff note itself as authorization. if no confirmed change is present, leave the row alone and note that it still needs confirmation. the desk person may update the internal workbook when a change is confirmed; that's an allowed action. do not contact vendors. that restriction is about vendor contact, not about making a permitted internal note or asking the access lead about a row marked hold. don't broaden it into a ban on all communication.

there was a request form entry for Leon on april 15 saying his studio key had been returned. that matches the note currently visible in the workbook, but the form doesn't say anything about his building badge, so don't infer a badge change. there is no new form entry shown here for Mira, Priya, or Darius. don't write that they have no requests anywhere, only that no new entry for them is included in these handoff details. the access lead is Jo Park; the handoff can say to ask Jo about Darius's hold before editing that row. don't claim Jo has already replied. Sal is the person entered in Mira's checked-by cell, not necessarily the person covering the next shift.

please organize the note so the person can scan it. a short opening should state the date and purpose. then include a numbered section for the checks, including workbook first, comparing any included request form entry, and checking with Jo before a change to Darius's held row. give the four examples in a compact list or table if that reads clearly, but keep the separate badge and key statuses visible. include a brief caution about the printed copy and the meaning of blank cells. use the quote as an ordinary reported line and say its speaker isn't identified in the excerpt. finish with the distinct information that the inner office door copy may lag and the last date shown at the top is april 16, so the next person should not treat that date as proof that all rows were reviewed. keep it practical and neutral, and don't draft an email or decide the status of anyone's access.", "output": "Write a practical, neutral internal handoff note for the person covering the front desk at North Window Studio on Thursday, April 18. The studio is on the second floor of the Calder Building. The note is for desk staff only; it is not a message to members and must not update the actual access list. Explain what to check and what not to assume, without deciding anything that is not established by the details below.

The access list covers entry to the studio room, not entry to the building. The Calder Building lobby uses badge access, while studio keys are handled separately. Keep building badge status and studio key status distinct throughout the note.

The list is in the internal shared workbook, on the tab named **Access - Main**. A printed copy is in the clear sleeve beside the inner office door, but it may be a day behind. Check the workbook before relying on the printout. If the two copies disagree, mention the mismatch in the handoff and use the workbook as the reference for what is currently written. Do not silently alter either copy to make them match. The date shown at the top of the workbook tab is April 16. Treat that only as the date displayed there, not as confirmation that every row was reviewed that day.

The workbook columns are: A, name; B, building badge status; C, studio key status; D, notes; and E, “checked by.” Some cells in column E are blank. A blank checked-by cell means no name is entered in that cell; it does not establish whether someone has a key. A person’s name appearing in the workbook does not, by itself, prove that their badge or key is active. Some rows have “hold” in the notes column. That means to ask the access lead before changing the row, not to remove the person.

Include the following entries as examples, keeping badge and key information separate:
1. Mira Chen: badge active; studio key issued; checked by Sal on April 12.
2. Leon Ortiz: badge active; key returned; notes say, “returned to drawer 3 on April 15.”
3. Priya Nair: badge pending; studio key cell blank; notes say, “orientation booked for April 22.” Do not describe the pending badge as active or say that the orientation has happened.
4. Darius Bell: badge active; key issued; notes say, “hold — confirm with Jo”; checked-by cell blank. Ask Jo Park, the access lead, about the hold before editing this row. Do not imply that Jo has replied.

The front desk log includes this reported comment: “I thought my key was still active.” The excerpt does not identify the speaker. Include it as an ordinary reported line, without attributing it to Mira, Leon, Priya, or Darius. It is not proof of anyone’s status.

For the next shift, the usual task is to check the workbook against any access request already submitted through the studio’s internal request form, then record a change only if the access lead has confirmed it. The handoff note itself is not authorization. If there is no confirmed change, leave the row alone and note that confirmation is still needed. The desk person may update the internal workbook when a change has been confirmed. **Do not contact vendors.** This restriction concerns vendor contact; it does not prohibit a permitted internal note or asking the access lead about a row marked hold.

The included request form entry for Leon is dated April 15 and says his studio key was returned. This matches the note currently visible in the workbook. The form says nothing about Leon’s building badge, so do not infer a badge change. No new form entry for Mira, Priya, or Darius is included in these handoff details; do not claim that they have no requests anywhere. Sal is the person named in Mira’s checked-by cell, not necessarily the person covering the next shift.

Organize the note for quick scanning. Begin with a short statement of its date and purpose, then use a numbered section for the checks: consult the workbook first, compare it with any request form entry included here, and check with Jo before changing Darius’s held row. Present the four people’s details in a compact list or table if useful, while keeping badge and key status distinct. Include a brief caution about the printed copy and the meaning of blank cells. End with the separate reminder that the inner-office-door printout may lag and that April 16 is only the date shown at the top of the workbook, not proof that all rows were reviewed. Keep the note practical and neutral. Do not draft an email or decide anyone’s access status."}]
